claims.text: In tungsten-based plasma-facing alloys, high-temperature plastic strain and toughness are governed by the stability and distribution of nanometer-scale oxide dispersions.
Nanometer-scale oxide dispersions pin grain boundaries.
Nanometer-scale oxide dispersions impede dislocation climb.
Nanometer-scale oxide dispersions retard grain-boundary sliding.
Standard powder metallurgy without intentional oxide dispersions produces a homogeneous tungsten-alloy microstructure with typical grain sizes.
Mechanical alloying with an oxide precursor, followed by consolidation and heat treatment, can create a uniform oxide dispersion in tungsten.
The intervention will produce nanometer-scale oxide particles at grain boundaries and within grains.
Oxide dispersions stabilize dislocation structures at high temperature.
Oxide dispersions reduce the rate of diffusional creep, particularly creep involving dislocation climb.
Oxide dispersions inhibit rapid grain-boundary migration.
Suppressing creep and grain-boundary migration produces a more uniform distribution of plastic strain.
A more uniform distribution of plastic strain improves toughness.
Relative to tungsten processed without intentionally introduced oxides, oxide-dispersed tungsten will exhibit greater high-temperature elongation to failure.
Relative to tungsten processed without intentionally introduced oxides, oxide-dispersed tungsten will exhibit improved high-temperature toughness.
Oxides improve ductility and toughness by reducing localized deformation and delaying catastrophic failure.
The proposed mechanism is expected to apply at approximately 800°C to 1500°C when creep and grain-boundary dynamics dominate deformation.
The proposed mechanism may not apply at lower temperatures or in substantially different alloy systems.
Oxide size, volume fraction, and spatial distribution affect the magnitude of the proposed benefit.
Grain size and other processing-dependent microstructural features may confound attribution of mechanical changes to the oxide dispersion.
